articles.title: Bluey’s Daley Pearson on how losing his brother inspired his new film: ‘He was the best thing ever to me’
articles.summary: Allen, the first live-action film from Pearson’s Ludo Studio, follows a man who met an alien as a kid – and becomes obsessed with bringing him back. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email.
body: If, for whatever reason, you want to feel a bit sad, think too hard about what Elliott from ET would have been like as an adult. Or Coraline, or Matilda, or Chihiro, or those kids in Mary Poppins. The most amazing thing that ever happened in their lives – magic nanny, alien friend, psychic abilities, otherworldly adventures – was already over when they were kids. If that bad Harry Potter play taught us anything, they probably all grew into loser adults.

There are a lot of nods to ET in Allen (“pretty aggressive nods,” Pearson laughs) – obviously the premise but also the score and even the poster, which features Allen and Petey’s fingers reaching to one another, and a floating Cheezel in the middle.
When I tell him that ET is among my favourite films, the 42-year-old winces. “Oh, no,” he says, rubbing his chin. “OK, we’ll talk about that.”

articles.title: Cineplex Boards Sanfic Title ‘La Residencia’ From ‘Algo Azul’ Director Mariel García Spooner
articles.summary: Latin American distributor Cineplex has picked up both North and South American sales rights to “La Residencia,” Mariel Garcia Spooner’s follow up to hit “Algo Azul.” “La Resdemcia” has just participated in the Sanfic Industria’s WIP Iberoamericana section, a competition of films from Latin…
body: Directed by Panamanian filmmaker García Spooner, the dramedy follows three women friends in their mid-sixties who join forces in order to jointly face their money troubles and reinvent their future by creating a social club for seniors.

Said Cineplex managing partner Diana Dudek, who works alongside co-founder-general manager Elba McAllister: “We have known Mariel for several years and have been working with her since her first film, ‘Algo Azul.’ We like her way of telling entertaining, relatable stories with a deeper underlying message.”

“With ‘La Residencia,’ from the moment we read the screenplay, we immediately connected with the story of these three friends who, at a more mature stage of their lives, decide to reinvent themselves and move forward together.”

The dramedy’s development trajectory includes it participation at Málaga WIP, after which it won the Latino Film Institute Work in Progress finishing fund at Laliff 2026, presented in collaboration with Amazon MGM Studios. In addition, Barcelona-based Only Postproduction boarded the project to support its color grading, following a connection established during Mafiz.

articles.title: Box Office: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Roars With $31 Million Debut, ‘Cat in the Hat’ Fizzles With $20 Million
articles.summary: The Cat in the Hat was no match for the mighty Godzilla. “Godzilla Minus Zero” climbed to the top of box office charts with $31.6 million from 3,254 theaters, a roaring start for a foreign-language epic in North America.
body: “We’re so happy to see audiences embrace ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ at an unprecedented scale for an international film,” says Chance Huskey, VP of distribution for Gkids, which distributed the movie in the U.S. The movie was produced by Japan’s Toho. “This landmark release is the result of a thoughtful campaign by Gkids and Toho that emphasized the ‘must-see’ intensity of the theatrical experience.”

“Godzilla Minus Zero” built on the success of the prior kaiju adventure, 2023’s “Godzilla Minus One.” That sci-fi epic secured a better-than-expected $11.4 million start and powered to $57 million in North America and $113 million globally, in addition to winning a visual effects Oscar. Directed by Takashi Yamazaki, the movie takes place two years after the previous installment as Godzilla regenerates and resurfaces to combat a new monster that’s tormenting postwar Japan.

“This is a soft opening,” Gross says. “However, family animation does extremely well in ancillary windows, earning more in digital sales and rental, streaming and TV licensing than in theatrical. That is where the film should recover its costs.”

articles.title: ‘I’ve seen people in my neighbourhood pulled out of their cars’: Ava DuVernay on the cruelty and brutality of Trump’s America
articles.summary: Ten years after her landmark political documentary 13th, the film-maker delivers a follow-up on the 14th amendment – and the Trump administration’s attempts to dismantle birthright citizenship.
body: When I ask Ava DuVernay how she kept her focus while making her new film – or how anyone does, when the onslaught of news, fake news and disputed facts seems designed to overwhelm – she starts to answer, then stops. Her eyes have filled with tears.

“I just got emotional, as you said that, because it was the film that saved me,” she says. “It’s been a very tough two years. I live in Los Angeles, and I’ve seen people in my neighbourhood pulled out of their cars. The lady who sells flowers next to my office was there one day, and the next day she wasn’t. People I know personally are literally hiding in their houses, like Anne Frank vibes … So when I would feel the rage and the fear, I put it into the film … And I just … I was doing something.”

articles.title: Taiwan’s Content Agency and Partners Put $180 Million Into 27 Projects, From an ‘Our Blues’ Remake to an Off-Broadway Musical
articles.summary: The Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA) and its partners have invested in 27 projects, backed by NT$5.64 billion ($180 million) in total, including NT$740 million ($23.7 million) from the agency and NT$4.9 billion ($157 million) in private capital, TAICCA chair Sue Wang said at the Taiwan…
body: Enjoy Entertainment, a partnership between TAICCA and Taiwanese telecom Far EasTone, said it had invested in 15 projects in its first 10 months: eight in film and TV and seven in music and live events. They include horror film “The Rope Curse 4: Kuntilanak,” which took NT$80 million ($2.6 million) at the Taiwanese box office, a franchise record, and VMTheatre Company’s “Don’t Cry, Dancing Girls the Musical,” billed at the event as the first Taiwanese musical to reach Off-Broadway.

On the music side, Enjoy developed the ID. Music Festival with Spotify, which brought 14 Taiwanese acts to two stages in the streamer’s first collaboration with a Taiwanese music event. It also highlighted “Her Voice,” a concert featuring five female performers from Taiwan and South Korea, and indie band Shallow Levée’s “Speak in Silence” project, which pairs the band’s 10th-anniversary album with collaborations with Japanese and Korean musicians and a planned tour of about 50 shows across Taiwan and eight other Asian countries.
Enjoy is also behind an immersive project marking 25 years of work by Taiwanese picture-book artist Jimmy Liao.

articles.title: The Right to Disobey: Sebastián Lelio (1974- 2026)
articles.summary: A tribute to the director of "A Fantastic Woman," "Gloria," and more.
body: Gloria’s body sways to the music. She’s taken off her glasses and mustered the courage to step into the dance floor. What begins as a succession of shy, awkward moves soon becomes a spontaneous celebration of autonomy for a middled-aged woman coming into her own at long last. Her outburst of self-assurance, ignoring what the world might think of her, illustrates a transformation. She’s been pushed around long enough. That’s over now.

Such determination to defend one’s dignity is also present in the rage that a trans woman displays when stumping on the car of the people who’ve dehumanized her for falling in love. And it’s in the incandescent desire that pushes an Orthodox Jewish wife to defy her dogma and surrender to an “illicit” kiss. It’s through these moments of transgression that Sebastián Lelio, the lauded Chilean filmmaker who died on Friday at age 52, molded many of his characters into relatable, yet heroic figures confronting intimate human battles.

articles.title: THR Visionary: 5 Janusz Kaminski Shots
articles.summary: The cinematographer, this year’s THR Visionary Award honoree, always lets film follow function, choosing a visual style to match the story being told.
body: Try to find a signature Janusz Kaminski “look” and you’ll come up empty. Yes, he likes backlighting and has a penchant for smoke and film-noir style. But the Polish-born cameraman, winner of the 2026 THR Visionary Award for excellence in cinematography, has spent three decades making images that bend to the story rather than the other way around.

Steven Spielberg’s Holocaust drama was shot in stark black-and-white. The choice wasn’t nostalgic but a way of conjuring newsreels and documentary record, with a handheld immediacy that keeps the audience in the room with the horror. Kaminski’s hard, contrasty lighting, harsh shadows and drifting smoke owe a debt to German Expressionism and postwar European cinema. Against this monochrome, the lone splash of color, the little girl’s red coat, lands as one of the most devastating images in modern film. It won him his first Oscar.
points: The cinematographer, this year’s THR Visionary Award honoree, always lets film follow function, choosing a visual style to match the story being told.

articles.title: 25 Best Directors Of All Time, Ranked
articles.summary: Trying to determine the 25 best directors of all time might seem like an impossible task, but we took a shot at it. Who is your all time favorite?
body: Ranking the best directors of all time is a formidable task. How do you weigh a director's output against their influence? Ultimately, the question is who has left the most lasting impression on film culture, and why.

Making a list like this also means confronting the industry's realities. You'll notice a dismal underrepresentation of directors of color, women, and queer filmmakers compared to the overwhelming majority of entries: white men.

Hollywood, and the filmmaking industry writ large, have historically diminished the voices of marginalized filmmakers, limiting their opportunities to create, distribute, and receive recognition for their work. When those opportunities have disproportionately gone to the same insular group, it's no surprise their work has come to dominate the cinematic canon. Hopefully, future renditions of this list will reflect a greater appreciation of historically overlooked filmmakers and the continued emergence of exciting, diverse voices pushing the medium forward.
For now, the directors on this list reflect film history's achievements and the inequities that have shaped it. Here are the 25 best directors of all time, ranked.

articles.title: Before Ghost Rider, Nicolas Cage Nearly Played A Very Different Marvel Superhero
articles.summary: Nicolas Cage has played superheroes like Ghost Rider, but he wanted to portray another Marvel hero in a movie long before they became an A-lister.
body: Nicolas Cage is an absolute legend. Along with his Oscar-winning turn in "Leaving Las Vegas" and roles in hits like "National Treasure," he's also played some superheroes in his day. Perhaps most notably, he played Ghost Rider in a pair of films released in 2007 and 2012. This came about years after Cage's "Superman Lives" was canceled. But before he suited up as Johnny Blaze, he almost portrayed another, very different hero from the pages of Marvel Comics.

In a 1997 report from Variety going over the "mania" surrounding Marvel movies in development at that time, it was revealed that Cage was still "firmly" attached to star as "his favorite "Marvel hero," Iron Man. Indeed, more than a decade before Robert Downey Jr. would take on the role as Tony Stark, it was Cage who was being eyed to bring the Marvel Comics hero to life. "Iron Man" became the unlikely superhero that changed Hollywood forever, so Cage taking on the role could have literally rewritten this chapter in cinema history.

articles.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Powers $31M in Historic Box Office Launch Against Subdued ‘Cat in the Hat’
articles.summary: The sequel to 2023's 'Godzilla Minus One' made noise as 'Ramayana' and 'Wild Horse Nine' also debuted.
body: Godzilla Minus Zero is king of the box office in its opening weekend as the sequel feature tallies the biggest launch in its distributor’s history with nearly three times the debut of predecessor Godzilla Minus One.

Godzilla Minus Zero added $31.4 million internationally, including $17 million in Japan. Filmmaker Takashi Yamazaki ‘s sequel to 2023’s Oscar-winning Godzilla Minus One earned an A CinemaScore from audiences and performed well above the distributor’s projected opening in the mid-$20 millions.

Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe and Min Tanaka star in the new movie that carries a reported budget in the mid-teens. It centers on postwar Japan dealing with attacks from the three-headed Ghidorah and the possibility of Godzilla’s return. Godzilla Minus Zero holds an impressive 90 percent critics approval on Rotten Tomatoes, along with a 96 from audiences, with The Hollywood Reporter chief film critic David Rooney calling it a “thrilling jolt of marauding monster action.”
